stories.headline: US March CPI Surges to 3.3% as Iran War Energy Shock Drives Biggest Monthly Spike in 4 Years

key_facts.fact: US CPI rose 0.9% month-on-month and 3.3% year-on-year in March, the largest annual increase since May 2024 and biggest monthly jump in nearly four years
key_facts.excerpt: The consumer price index (CPI) increased by 3.3 percent year on year in March as energy costs soared, registering the largest spike in nearly two years

key_facts.fact: Energy prices surged 10.9% in March, with gasoline jumping 21.2% — the largest single-month gasoline increase on record — accounting for nearly three-quarters of the overall monthly CPI increase
key_facts.excerpt: Motor fuel – diesel and gasoline – surged 21.5%, the hottest monthly gain on record. (The data goes back to the 1960s.)

key_facts.fact: Core CPI (excluding food and energy) rose a modest 0.2% month-on-month and 2.6% year-on-year, suggesting the inflation spike is energy-driven rather than broad-based
key_facts.excerpt: so-called 'core' CPI stood at 2.6% year-on-year and 0.2% month-on-month, both slower than forecast

key_facts.fact: University of Michigan consumer sentiment plunged to 47.6 in April from 53.3 in March — the lowest level since the survey began in 1952; 12-month inflation expectations surged to 4.8% from 3.8%
key_facts.excerpt: Consumer sentiment plunged 11% in April… the lowest level since the start of data collection in 1952. Expectations for inflation in 12 months rose to 4.8% from 3.8% in February

key_facts.fact: Gasoline prices averaged $4.15/gallon nationally, up roughly 40% from $2.98 before the Iran war began, according to AAA
key_facts.excerpt: Gas prices averaged $4.15 a gallon nationwide Friday, up from $2.98 on the day before the war began, according to motor club AAA

key_facts.fact: San Francisco Fed President Mary Daly said oil shock extends the timeline for getting inflation to 2%, and the Fed may hold rates steady; she placed lower probability on a rate hike than on a cut or hold
key_facts.excerpt: We had work to do before we had the oil price shock; with the oil price shock, the work just takes longer

stories.headline: Artemis II Crew Splashes Down in Pacific After Historic 10-Day Moon Flyby Mission

key_facts.fact: NASA's Orion capsule 'Integrity' splashed down in the Pacific Ocean off San Diego at 8:07 PM EDT on April 10, ending the 10-day Artemis II mission — the first crewed voyage beyond low Earth orbit in over 53 years
key_facts.excerpt: The splashdown, which happened in the Pacific Ocean off the coast of San Diego at 8:07 p.m. EDT / 5:07 p.m. PDT, followed a harrowing and dangerous reentry

key_facts.fact: All four crew members — NASA astronauts Reid Wiseman, Victor Glover, Christina Koch, and Canadian Space Agency astronaut Jeremy Hansen — were recovered safely and reported healthy
key_facts.excerpt: NASA reported that a navy medical officer who briefly checked the astronauts aboard the capsule found them all to be healthy

key_facts.fact: The crew set a new human spaceflight distance record of 252,756 miles from Earth during the lunar flyby, surpassing Apollo 13's record by more than 4,100 miles
key_facts.excerpt: On 6 April, the spacecraft reached its maximum distance from Earth - 406,771km (252,756 miles)- during the lunar flyby, breaking the previous record

key_facts.fact: The capsule re-entered at nearly Mach 33 (about 24,661 mph), enduring temperatures above 5,000°F on its heat shield — the first crewed test of Orion's heat shield, which had known design flaws from an unmanned 2022 flight
key_facts.excerpt: Re-entry is always one of the riskiest parts of spaceflight, but that was particularly true for Artemis II, because Orion's heat shield — the critical layer that protects astronauts from extreme temperatures — had known design flaws

key_facts.fact: Glover became the first Black astronaut, Koch the first woman, and Hansen the first non-American to fly to the Moon; the mission paves the way for Artemis III (2027) and a lunar landing on Artemis IV (2028)
key_facts.excerpt: Glover, Koch and Hansen also made history as the first Black astronaut, the first woman and first non-American to fly around the moon

stories.headline: Vance Arrives in Islamabad for Iran Peace Talks as Tehran Sets Preconditions and Trump Threatens War

key_facts.fact: VP JD Vance departed for Islamabad on April 10 with envoy Steve Witkoff and Jared Kushner for Pakistan-mediated peace talks with Iran, telling reporters 'We're looking forward to the negotiation. I think it's going to be positive'
key_facts.excerpt: U.S. Vice President J.D. Vance departed for Islamabad on Friday to participate in Pakistan-mediated peace talks to end the Iran war

key_facts.fact: Iran's parliamentary speaker Ghalibaf posted that 'a ceasefire in Lebanon and the release of Iran's blocked assets' must be fulfilled before negotiations can begin; his delegation arrived in Islamabad with security, political, military, economic, and legal teams
key_facts.excerpt: 'These two matters must be fulfilled before negotiations begin,' he wrote... the Iranian delegation led by Parliament Speaker Mohammad Bagher Qalibaf arrived in Islamabad

key_facts.fact: Trump told the New York Post the US is 'loading up the ships with the best weapons ever made' during the ceasefire pause, warning 'if we don't have a deal, we will be using them'
key_facts.excerpt: We have a reset going. We're loading up the ships with the best ammunition, the best weapons ever made—even better than what we did previously

key_facts.fact: The Strait of Hormuz remains effectively blocked with 68+ loaded tankers trapped in the Persian Gulf; only about 22 ships have passed since the ceasefire on April 7, versus 100+ per day pre-war
key_facts.excerpt: More than 68 loaded tankers are trapped in the Persian Gulf, carrying around 16 billion litres of oil. This blockade halts the normal daily transit of around 20 million barrels of crude

key_facts.fact: Israel and Lebanon will hold direct negotiations starting Tuesday in Washington; more than 300 people were killed in Israeli strikes on Beirut the day the Iran ceasefire was announced, and at least 1,953 have died in Lebanon total
key_facts.excerpt: negotiations between Israel and Lebanon were expected to begin Tuesday in the U.S. capital... The day the truce was announced, Israel pounded Beirut with airstrikes, killing more than 300 people

key_facts.fact: More than 3,000 people have been killed in Iran and 13 US service members have died since the war began roughly six weeks ago
key_facts.excerpt: More than 3,000 people have been killed in Iran, a top Iranian officer told the state-run Iran newspaper... 13 U.S. service members have been killed

stories.headline: Xi Jinping Meets Taiwan's KMT Leader in Beijing — First Such Talks in a Decade

key_facts.fact: Chinese President Xi Jinping met Kuomintang chairwoman Cheng Li-wun at Beijing's Great Hall of the People on April 10 — the first official meeting between sitting CCP and KMT leaders since November 2016
key_facts.excerpt: This was the first official meeting between the sitting heads of the Chinese Communist Party and the KMT, which favors closer ties with Beijing, in almost a decade

key_facts.fact: Xi said 'we need peace, we need development, we need communication and we need cooperation' and declared he 'absolutely would not tolerate' Taiwan independence
key_facts.excerpt: Compatriots on both sides are both Chinese, and we need peace, we need development, we need communication and we need cooperation. This is a common wish

key_facts.fact: The meeting comes weeks before a planned May summit between Xi and Trump in Beijing, where Taiwan is expected to be high on the agenda alongside U.S. arms sales to the island
key_facts.excerpt: The meeting comes ahead of a summit in Beijing with President Donald Trump planned for May, where Xi is likely to bring up his opposition to U.S. arms sales to Taiwan

key_facts.fact: Taiwan's defense ministry detected 16 Chinese warplanes flying near the island during the same hours Xi and Cheng were meeting on Friday morning
key_facts.excerpt: Taiwan's defence ministry said on Saturday that it spotted 16 Chinese warplanes operating near the island the previous day, around the same time China's president was meeting the Taiwanese opposition leader

key_facts.fact: Cheng's KMT has been blocking a stalled $40 billion defense spending bill in Taiwan's parliament; an April poll showed the KMT commands less than a third of popular support
key_facts.excerpt: A survey in April showed the KMT has less than a third of popular support

stories.headline: Zelensky Confirms Ukraine Shot Down Iranian Drones in Multiple Gulf States, Signs 10-Year Deals

key_facts.fact: Zelensky revealed on April 10 that Ukrainian military experts successfully shot down Iranian Shahed-type drones 'in several countries' in the Middle East using domestically produced interceptor drones and electronic warfare systems
key_facts.excerpt: Did we destroy Iranian Shaheds? Yes, we did. Did we do it in just one country? No, in several. And in my view, this is a success.

key_facts.fact: Ukraine sent more than 200 experts to the Middle East and signed 10-year security agreements with Saudi Arabia, UAE, and Qatar; talks are underway with Oman, Kuwait, and Bahrain
key_facts.excerpt: Ukraine also sent more than 200 experts to the Middle East… We've reached agreements on 10-year deals with three countries

key_facts.fact: In exchange for drone defense expertise, Ukraine receives Patriot PAC-2 and PAC-3 interceptors for its own air defense, along with oil and diesel supplies and financial agreements
key_facts.excerpt: Zelenskyy offered Kyiv's expertise and inexpensive interceptor technology for downing Shahed drones to the Gulf states in exchange for the Pac-2 and Pac-3 interceptors that Ukraine needed

key_facts.fact: Zelensky described the deployment as 'not about a training mission or exercises, but about support in building a modern air defence system that can actually work'
key_facts.excerpt: This was not about a training mission or exercises, but about support in building a modern air defence system that can actually work

key_facts.fact: Zelensky also confirmed Ukraine's military will participate in consultations on the future operation of the Strait of Hormuz
key_facts.excerpt: Ukraine's military would take part in consultations on the future operation of the Strait of Hormuz

stories.headline: China to Ban Sulphuric Acid Exports From May as Hormuz Blockade Cuts Global Sulphur Supply

key_facts.fact: China has notified producers it will halt sulphuric acid exports from May, hitting metals and fertilizer industries already strained by Hormuz-related raw material shortages; the ban could last throughout 2026
key_facts.excerpt: CHINA has indicated it will halt exports of sulphuric acid from May, hitting metals and fertiliser industries already strained by raw material bottlenecks resulting from the Iran war

key_facts.fact: The Middle East produces one-third of the world's sulphur, a raw material for sulphuric acid used in copper extraction and phosphate fertilizers; the Strait of Hormuz blockade has cut off these shipments
key_facts.excerpt: The region produces one-third of the world's sulphur, a raw material used to make sulphuric acid that's essential for some copper extraction and phosphate fertilisers

key_facts.fact: Chile — the world's No. 1 copper producer — buys over 1 million tonnes of Chinese sulphuric acid annually; about one-fifth of Chilean copper output depends on sulphuric acid processing
key_facts.excerpt: Prices have already surged in Chile, which buys over one million tonnes of Chinese sulphuric acid every year. Around a fifth of the copper output in Chile – the world's No 1 producer – involves a type of processing that depends on sulphuric acid

key_facts.fact: China's move comes during peak crop-planting season and will further pressure copper-mining industries in Chile, the Democratic Republic of Congo, and Zambia
key_facts.excerpt: China's move to conserve sulphuric acid supplies during the peak crop-planting season will put further pressure on the market

sources.title: China moves to ban sulphuric acid exports as Iran war hits supply

stories.headline: FDA Rejects Replimune's Melanoma Drug RP1 for the Second Time, Triggering Job Cuts

key_facts.fact: The FDA on April 10 issued a second Complete Response Letter rejecting Replimune's RP1 (vusolimogene oderparepvec) for advanced melanoma, saying the data are 'insufficient to conclude substantial evidence of effectiveness'
key_facts.excerpt: the review team, as well as multiple agency leaders and subject matter experts, determined the data are 'insufficient to conclude substantial evidence of effectiveness'

key_facts.fact: In the IGNYTE trial, RP1 plus nivolumab showed a 34% response rate with a median duration of 24.8 months in patients whose melanoma progressed on anti-PD-1 therapy
key_facts.excerpt: In the IGNYTE trial, patients with confirmed progression on an anti-PD-1 based regimen who received RP1 plus nivolumab had a 34% response rate with a median duration of 24.8 months

key_facts.fact: A senior member of the prior FDA review team had publicly stated 'the BLA clinical team thought the applicant had provided adequate evidence' but leadership disagreed; a different review team was assigned for the resubmission
key_facts.excerpt: A senior member of the prior review team stated publicly that the 'BLA clinical team thought the applicant had provided adequate evidence to support contribution of effect of RP1 plus nivolumab but leadership did not agree'

key_facts.fact: Replimune announced it will eliminate jobs and substantially scale back US manufacturing; CEO Sushil Patel said the treatment 'will not be available — not because the medicine failed, because the system did'
key_facts.excerpt: we have no choice but to eliminate jobs, including substantially scaling back our U.S. based manufacturing operations. A treatment desperately needed by patients will not be available. Not because the medicine failed. Because the system did.

key_facts.fact: Replimune shares fell about 20% on the news; the case has become a flashpoint in the debate over FDA review standards under Vinay Prasad's leadership of the biologics division
key_facts.excerpt: Replimune shares fell about 20% in midday trading Friday
